{{nihongo|'''Sumiyoshi Shrine'''|住吉神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Chikuzen Province]].

There is a theory that it is the founder of {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine|Q11381857|qid=Q11381857}} located all over the country, and it is also considered one of the ``three great Sumiyoshi'' along with {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}} in Osaka and {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|ja|住吉神社 (下関市)|simple|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|zh|住吉神社 (下關市)|qid=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} in Shimonoseki.<ref>{{Cite book |Japanese book |editor=Mutsuhiko Mori |title=Number Dictionary |publisher=Tokyodo Publishing |year=1987 |page=135}}</ref>.This is a shrine dedicated to {{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013}}, the guardian deities of navigation. === Enshrined God ===
The following five deities are enshrined. </ref>. These five pillars are also collectively known as ``Sumiyoshi Gosho Okami.''

; Main enshrined deity
:* '''{{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Sotsutsu no Omikoto}}''' (Sotsutsu no Onomikoto)
:* '''{{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Nakatsutsuo no Mikoto}}''' (Nakatsutsuo no Mikoto)
:* '''{{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013|lt=Omotetsu Otoko no Mikoto}}''' (Uwatsutsu no Onomikoto)
: The above three pillars are collectively called "{{ill|Sumiyoshi sanjin|Q1114013|qid=Q1114013}}"<ref name="Yoshisho"/>.

; Deity enshrined
:* {{ill|Amaterasu|Q455602|qid=Q455602|lt=Amaterasu Omikami}} (Amaterasusume wolf)
:* {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}}

=== About the enshrined deity ===
{{Double image stack|right|Sumiyoshi-taisha, keidai-2.jpg|Sumiyoshi-jinja (Shimonoseki) Honden.JPG|200|{{Center|Top: {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}} ({{ill|Osaka Prefecture|Q122723|qid=Q122723}}{{ill|Osaka|Q35765|qid=Q35765}})<br />Bottom: {{ill|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|ja|住吉神社 (下関市)|simple|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shimonoseki)|zh|住吉神社 (下關市)|qid=Q11381858|lt=Sumiyoshi Shrine}} ({{ill|Yamaguchi Prefecture|Q127264|qid=Q127264}}{{ill|Shimonoseki|Q203308|qid=Q203308}})}}}}The main enshrined deities, the Sumiyoshi Sanjin, appear in two scenes in ``{{ill|Kojiki|Q813031|qid=Q813031}}'' and ``{{ill|Nihon Shoki|Q813935|qid=Q813935}}.'' One is the birth scene, where {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858}} (Izanagi no Mikoto), who returned from the land of Yomi, went to Ahakihara (Enohara) in Tachibana no Odo in Tsukushi-Hyuga to purify himself of the impurities.{{ill|Misogi|Q1936265|qid=Q1936265}} Accordingly, these three Sumiyoshi gods were born along with {{ill|Watatsumi|Q1474187|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi three gods}} (three sea gods) {{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=28-30}}{{Sfn|Shoki|1967|pp=94-95}}. Next, in the scene of {{ill|Empress Jingū|Q232803|qid=Q232803}} dispatching troops to Korea, Sumiyoshi possesses the empress and gives oracles to her, and the empress {{ill|Q1124943 5|qid=Q1124943 5|lt=By cooperating with the Sanhan Conquest}}, the conquest will be successful.{{Sfn|Kojiki|1963|pp=132-134}} "Nihonshoki" states that upon their return from Korea, there was an oracle, and that they built a shrine to enshrine the Sumiyoshi god {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Aratama}} in Anamon Yamada village, and a shrine to enshrine {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Watama}} in Nakakura Nagakyo, Otsunoki. (Shimonoseki City)|Q11381858|Sumiyoshi Shrine}}, compared to {{ill|Sumiyoshi-taisha|Q705949|qid=Q705949}} in Osaka) {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.On the other hand, in our company's origin story, we attribute this to Awagihara, where the Sumiyoshi deity was born. }}{{Refnest|group=Notes|Approximately 10 kilometers west of Sumiyoshi Shrine is Hyuga Pass, and approximately 10 kilometers northeast is Aoyagi (Awagi?), Koga City. It is also associated with place names such as Mt. Tachibana (Tachibana?) and the foothills of Mt. Bito (Odo?) to the north. }}. Among these theories, "Nihonshoki" <ref group="Hara"> "Nihonshoki" includes an article dated September 10, 9th year, 9th year of Emperor Chuai's reign, in the pre-Regency period of Empress Jingu. In </ref>, an article states that Empress Jingu ordered {{ill|Yosami no Otarumi|Q24899491|qid=Q24899491|lt=Yorami Agohiko Tarumi}} to be the Shinto priest of Sumiyoshi God before the Sanhan Conquest {{Sfn |Shoki|1967|pp=335-336}} is the founding record of our company, and from this it is said that it was the earliest of all Sumiyoshi Shrines to be built {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}.

There are various theories regarding the literal meaning of ``Tsutsunowo'' for the three Sumiyoshi deities, Sokozutsu no Mikoto, Nakazutsu no no Mikoto, and Omotzutsu no Mikoto. The word tutu is related to the evening moon, and refers to the evening moon, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=evening star}}, and the stars.As stars are used as guides for navigation, there are some theories that it refers to the god of the sea, {{Sfn|Kawaguchi|1993|p=148}}, a theory that it is seen as a ``Tsu man,'' a theory that sees ``tutu'' as a ship's cursed staff, and a tube that houses a ship's spirit. There is a theory that he is seen as a ``mametsu man'' in connection with the Tsutsu of Tsushima, and a theory that he is seen as a ``Tsutushimu'', a body with a weakened body that accompanies a voyage.

=== History ===

=== Founding ===
Shrine (Chikuzen Province Sumiyoshi Daimyojin Engi <ref> Shrine collection. Collection: {{Cite book |Japanese book |title={{ill|Shintō Taikei|Q11590923|qid=Q11590923}} Shrine Edition 44 - Chikuzen, Chikugo, Buzen, Bungo Province |publisher=Shinto Taikei Compilation Association |year=1982}}</ref>) compares the place where this Sumiyoshi Shrine is enshrined to the ancient site of Ahakihara, where the god Sumiyoshi was born.{{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}. With this, weThe company is said to be the ``Sumiyoshi Head Office'' or ``Japan's No. 1 Sumiyoshi Shrine,'' which has been the enshrined place since ancient times. It is based on the {{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}}{{Sfn|Ichinomiya system in medieval countries|2000|pp=576-577}}.
In the ``Ancient Map of Hakata,'' a medieval illustrated map, the site of our company is topographically located between the Hie River and the Naka River. (Kyushu)|Q11642765|Q11642765|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}} It appears to be located on the cape of Reizeitsu that juts out from the mouth of the Naka River, and it is believed that this area was a suitable place for the worship of the guardian god of navigation.{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}{{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}} Also, in "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Japanese Namesho}}", {{ill|Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|qid=Q1047664}}{{ill|Naka district|Q11642798|qid=Q11642798|lt=Naka District}} There is a mention of the ancient place name ``Kaifu-go'', which is thought to be common to the {{ill|Amabe Caste|Q55528867|qid=Q55528867|lt=Amajin tribe}} villages, and from the precincts there is a mention of {{jal from the {{ill|Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858}}. ink|Bronze halberd|Q11650186}} and {{ill|dōhoko|Q11650189|qid=Q11650189|lt=Bronze spear}} are said to have been excavated, so there is a theory that this area has been a sacred place for the Kaijin people since ancient times.{{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}.In addition, in the "Chikuzen Kuni Zoku Fudoki Shui", the original location of our company is {{ill|Arahito Shrine|Q85882377|qid=Q85882377}} ({{ill|Fukuoka Prefecture|Q123258|qid=Q123258}}{ {jalink|Nakagawa City|Q1206001}}). According to this legend, the current location of the Jinjin Shrine was along the coastline, and as the coastline receded, it was moved to the current location of Sumiyoshi, Hakata Ward. In the "Shikinaisha Investigation Report", there are ruins thought to belong to {{ill|Nakoku|Q600473|qid=Q600473}} (such as {{ill|Suguokamoto Site|Q11473236|qid=Q11473236}}) located between Sumiyoshi Shrine and Genjin Shrine. Therefore, there is a theory that the rituals of the two shrines have been connected since ancient times as a shrine located upstream and downstream of {{ill|Naka River (Tochigi Ibaraki)|Q1076983|qid=Q1076983}} {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Shikiuchi Shrine)|1978}}.

In the Shikigami Namecho|Q11064932|Shinmeicho}} (established in {{ill|927|Q30470|qid=Q30470}}), {{ill|Settsu Province|Q864163|qid=Q864163}} and {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Harima Province}}・{{ill|Nagato Province|Q907382|qid=Q907382}}・{{ill|Chikuzen Province|Q1047664|qid=Q1047664}}・{{ill|Iki Province|Q1052938|qid=Q1052938}}・{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Tsushima Province}}, there are descriptions of Sumiyoshi Shrines in each of them, so there is a theory that these shrines, including ours, had the intention of locating them at key points on the Korean route {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}. In this, Sumiyoshi was considered to be the national guardian deity of navigation because it was inseparable from the conquest tradition of Empress Jingu, and the {{jalink|Five Kings of Wa|Q There is also a theory that he was deeply involved in the military and diplomacy of {{ill|Yamato Kingship|Q2658252|qid=Q2658252}} from around 1152880}} {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}.

After the war, it was listed as {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.{{ill|Heisei era|Q234510|qid=Q234510}} From 2016 ({{ill|2004|Q2014|qid=Q2014}}), excavation surveys have begun around the precincts (Sumiyoshi Shrine ruins) {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine ruins 1st survey report|2006|p=6}}. In a total of three surveys up to 2014 ({{ill|2014|Q1999|qid=Q1999}}), the remains of a mansion from the medieval to early modern period were discovered along with artifacts related to rituals. Medieval mansion ruins discovered in Sumiyoshi, Hakata Ward! - About the third excavation survey of Sumiyoshi Shrine ruins -] (Fukuoka City homepage). </ref>, the orientation of the mansion site coincides with the current main shrine, and it was also confirmed that this orientation dates back to the first half of the Middle Ages {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine Ruins First Survey Report|2006|p=6}}.

=== Shinto priest/sharei ===
Shinto priests are the {{ill|Tengen (era)|Q1327101|qid=Q1327101|lt=Tengen}} 2nd year ({{ill|979|Q23784|qid=Q23784}}) According to the Daijo Kanfu, there was a Daiguji, and "{{ill|Azuma Kagami|ckb|ئازوما کاگامی|de|Azuma Kagami|fa|آزوما کاگامی|fr|Azuma kagami|id|Azuma Kagami|ja|吾妻鏡|ko|아즈마카가미|vi|Azuma Kagami|zh|吾妻鏡|qid=Q1042324}}" states that {{ill|Azuma Kagami|ckb|ئازوما کاگامی|de|Azuma Kagami|fa|آزوما کاگامی|fr|Azuma kagami|id|Azuma Kagami|ja|吾妻鏡|ko|아즈마카가미|vi|Azuma Kagami|zh|吾妻鏡|qid=Q1042324}} The name of the Saeki clan appears as a priest who also served |Minamoto no Yoritomo|Q242800}}{{sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Heibonsha)|2004}}, and after that, the Yokota clan, a descendant of the Saeki clan, was in charge for generations {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Gods)|1984}}. The shrine's territory appears to be ``Sumiyoshi-sho'' in literature, and its affiliation continued through changes such as Goshirakawa-inryo, Senyomon-inryo, Fushimi-inryo, and Imperial family territory {{Sfn|Sumiyoshi Shrine (Kadokawa)|1988}}.

Orie Yokota, the chief priest of the {{ill|Tenpō|Q1369045|qid=Q1369045}} era, revived Shinto rituals that had been forbidden by the {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|Q208766|qid=Q208766}}. Wish, {{ill|Hakozaki Shrine|Q714742|qid=Q714742}} and the chief priests of {{ill|Umi Hachiman-gū|Q924940|qid=Q924940}} and {{jalink|Kyoto|Q740 When he complained to the {{ill|Ichijō family|Q1535498|qid=Q1535498}} of 246}}, he was arrested and ordered to return home by the domain, and in 1833, he retired and {{ja link|Zashiki prison|Q11486150}}<ref>The Life of Chobei Omiwa, Yasukuni Ashitsu (Ashitsu Office, 2008) p42</ref>.

=== Precincts ===
[[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), honden.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main shrine (Important cultural property)}}{{small|The style of the shrine building is "Sumiyoshi-zukuri". }}]]
The area of the precincts is 8,107 tsubo (2.68 hectares) <ref name="Yoshisho"/>. Unlike Hakata, which is located on sand dunes, the area around the shrine grounds is located on the alluvial land of the Naka River.Among the shrine buildings in the precincts, the {{ill|Shinto architecture|Q3080012|qid=Q3080012|lt='''main shrine'''}} was built in the early {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} period. (Japan)|Q635245|Genna}}9 year ({{ill|1623|Q6818|qid=Q6818}}) Built by {{ill|Fukuoka Domain|Q208766|qid=Q208766|lt=Fukuoka feudal lord}}{{ill|Kuroda Nagamasa|Q950496|qid=Q950496}}. Along with {{ill|Shinmei-zukuri|Q930545|qid=Q930545}} and {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|Q387874|qid=Q387874}}, it is said to be an old shrine style.''{{jalink |Sumiyoshizo|Q3503635}}''''' {{Sfn|Inagaki|2000|p=174}}{{Sfn|Yonezawa|2016|pp=112-113}} will be adopted. It is {{ill|Kirizuma-style|Q13308575|qid=Q13308575}} with 4 girders (depth) and 2 beams (frontage), and the roof is {{ill|cypress bark roof|Q90373477|qid=Q90373477}}. The straight lines of the roof and the three {{ill|Bargeboard|Q4881511|qid=Q4881511}} and {{ill|chigi and katsuogi|Q87220234|qid=Q87220234|lt=chigi/kataogi}} reflect the ancient architecture. The pillars are painted vermilion and the wooden walls are painted white. {{Sfn|Seiji Okada|2011|pp=86-109}}. <ref name="Kuni Honden"/><ref>[http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t6&fields=f767&id=1307-4&bunrui=kuni_yuke_kenz_juyo Sumiyoshi Shrine Main Hall] (Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture''). </ref><ref name="fukuokacityhonden">[http://bunkazai.city.fukuoka.lg.jp/cultural_properties/detail/140 Sumiyoshi Shrine Main Hall] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties Protection Division ``Fukuoka City Cultural Properties''). </ref><ref name="historical book"/>.The {{ill|Shinto architecture|Q3080012|qid=Q3080012|lt='''haiden'''}} built in front of the main shrine is {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|Q855025|qid=Q855025}} and has a copper plate roof. === Sessha ===
There are a total of 8 Setsusha shrines, 2 Setsusha shrines and 6 Setsusha shrines<ref name="Yoshisho"/>.

=== Sessha ===
[[File:Sumiyoshi-jinja (Fukuoka), Shiga-jinja and Funarama-jinja.JPG|thumb|230px|right|{{center|Funatama Shrine (right) and Shiga Shrine (left)}}]]
* Funatama Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko no Mikoto}}. Regular festival: September 9th.
* Shiga Shrine - Enshrined Deity: {{ill|Watatsumi|Q1474187|qid=Q1474187|lt=Watatsumi Three Gods}}. Regular festival: June 1st.

* Hitomaru Shrine - Enshrined deity: {{ill|Kakinomoto no Hitomaro|Q380818|qid=Q380818|lt=Kakimoto Hitomaro}}. Regular festival: March 18th.
* Amatsu Shrine - Enshrined outside the west gate. Enshrined deity: {{ill|Izanagi|Q813858|qid=Q813858|lt=Izanagi Okami}}. Regular festival: April 22nd.

=== Main festivals ===
;Oiina Festival
: "Follow me." January 7th. As a prayer for the prosperity of the imperial family and the nation, the Onisube and Uso-kaeshi rituals are held <ref name="Winter">[http://chikuzen-sumiyoshi.or.jp/event/winter.html Winter festivals and events] (official website)</ref><ref name="Historical Record"/>.
; Oda Festival
: "Ondasai". March 7th. A sowing ritual is held as a prayer for a rich harvest.
; Shiohi Festival
: "Shiohisai". April 3rd. A mikoshi (portable shrine) is performed to pray for safe navigation and a bountiful catch. It is said that in the past, when the sea spread out in front of the gates, the shrine was celebrated by boat, but now it is performed on land.
; Nagoshi Grand Festival
: “I want to relax.” July 30th to August 1st. It is a Shinto ritual related to the birth of Sumiyoshi deity during the purification of Izani no Mikoto, and rituals such as passing through grass rings and floating puppets are performed to purify impurities.
; Reitaisai: Also known as ``Sumo-kai Taisai'' or simply ``Sumo-kai Festival.'' October 12th to 14th. The most important festival at Sumiyoshi Shrine. It is said that the name originates from the fact that when Empress Jingu returned from Korea, she dedicated sumo and {{ill|Yabusame|Q1886157|qid=Q1886157}} to the deity Sumiyoshi as a thank you for the blessings of the gods. At the festival, in addition to a procession of children, yabusame and youth sumo are offered.
; Shooting Festival
: "Hoshasai". November 7th. This Shinto ritual is said to have its origins in the {{ill|Dazaifu (government)|Q144845|qid=Q144845}} official who, during the {{ill|Emperor Yōzei|Q349280|qid=Q349280}}'s offering in 878, performed a walking shot in the southwest (Urakimon) direction as a reward for the miraculous powers of the god Sumiyoshi who had ended the disaster of foreign pirates. A shooting ceremony is held in front of the shrine to pray for the protection of the nation.

=== Cultural assets ===

=== Important cultural property (designated by the country) ===
* Main shrine (building) - {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}} early period. Designated on April 13, 1922 (Taisho 11)

=== Fukuoka Prefecture designated cultural property ===
* Tangible cultural properties <ref> [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/koukosiryo.html Archaeological materials list] (Fukuoka City cultural properties <personal site>). </ref>
** 6-piece copper sword (archaeological material)
**: {{ill|dōka|Q11650186|qid=Q11650186}} from the middle of the {{ill|Yayoi period|Q207858|qid=Q207858}}. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building, but the condition and location of the excavation are unknown. It is medium-slender, with a total length of around 34 centimeters. Designated October 29, 1958 <ref>[http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-112&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko [Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture'']. </ref><ref name="Explanation board"/>.
** 5 copper hoko (archaeological material)**: {{ill|dōhoko|Q11650189|qid=Q11650189|lt=bronze spear}} from the middle of the Yayoi period. It is said that it was excavated from behind the shrine building like the bronze dagger, but its condition and location are unknown. Designated October 29, 1958 <ref>[http://www.fsg.pref.fukuoka.jp/bunka/contents_detail.asp?table=t61&fields=f2293&id=1307-113&bunrui=kenn_yuke_biju_koko Dohoko] (Fukuoka Social Education Network ``Cultural Properties of Fukuoka Prefecture''). </ref><ref name="Explanation board"/>.

=== Cultural property designated by Fukuoka City ===
* Tangible Cultural Properties <ref> [https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/kenzoubutu.html List of Tangible Cultural Properties Buildings] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties <Personal Site>). </ref><ref>[https://www.asahi-net.or.jp/~ri5t-mk/itiran/komonjo.html List of books, classics, and old books] (Fukuoka City Cultural Properties <personal site>). </ref>
** Nohgakuden (building) - Built in 1938. Designated on March 23, 2000.
** Karamon (building) - Built in the Edo period. Designated on March 18, 2010.
** Matsuka Wakashu Volume 5 Volume 1 (Books, Classics, Old Books) - A collection of poems from the end of the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}. Designated on March 30, 1987.
** 27 Sumiyoshi Shrine documents (books, classics, old books) - Documents from the Kamakura period onwards. Designated on March 30, 1987.
